reviewer: Captain (A-lane; sections bound from the committed OR memo's controlling text, not a counsel approval)
purpose: The Oregon packet specification carries seven legal sections, all unbound, and its generator says in terms that a generator does not write them. This record writes the ones the controlling text supports and leaves the rest unbound. Five are bound; two are not, and the two are the point.
vehicleQuestionIsClosed: The form and vehicle question is settled and is not reopened here: the OJD Criminal Set-Aside (Adult Cases) packet, retained at REV-2026-01, is the statewide set ORS 137.225(12) requires the State Court Administrator to publish. This record binds section text only.

filingDestination.statement: File the motion and the proposed order in the Oregon circuit court for the county in which the person was arrested, cited or charged. Where more than one county is involved, each county is a separate filing.
filingDestination.basisQuote: The circuit court in the county in which the person was arrested, cited or charged. ORS 137.225(1)(c).
filingDestination.timingNote: The motion may be filed at any time after 60 days from the prosecutor's declination. That is a precondition to filing rather than a post-filing step, and it belongs to eligibility, not to this section.
filingDestination.multipleCountiesStop: Multiple counties is a recorded stop condition, so the packet states the rule and does not attempt to compose a multi-county filing.

feeAndWaiver.statement: There is no court filing fee for this motion. The Department of State Police charges a record-check fee not exceeding its actual cost, and where only one record check is performed it may charge only one fee regardless of how many counties are filed in. The prosecuting attorney may not charge the person a fee. A fee waiver is not applicable, because there is no court filing fee to waive.
feeAndWaiver.basisQuote: No court filing fee: ORS 137.225(1)(g) provides that a person filing a motion under the section is not required to pay the filing fee established under ORS 21.135. The Department of State Police charges a record-check fee not exceeding the actual cost, and where only one record check is performed it may charge only one fee regardless of the number of counties filed in. The prosecuting attorney may not charge a fee.
feeAndWaiver.whatItDoesNotSay: The OSP record-check fee amount is not stated and is not written. It is the department's actual cost, which the packet describes rather than quantifies.

serviceAndNotice.statement: Serve a copy of the motion on the office of the prosecuting attorney who had authority to prosecute the charge, no accusatory instrument having been filed. The prosecuting attorney has 120 days from the date the motion was filed to object and to notify the court and the person. The prosecuting attorney may not charge the person a fee for performing these requirements. Separately, a full set of fingerprints is forwarded to the Department of State Police.
serviceAndNotice.basisQuote: ORS 137.225(2)(a): a copy of the motion is served on the office of the prosecuting attorney who prosecuted the matter, or who had authority to prosecute if no accusatory instrument was filed. Under ORS 137.225(2)(e) the prosecuting attorney may not charge the person a fee for performing these requirements.
serviceAndNotice.fingerprintsAreParticipantWork: The participant is fingerprinted and pays the department's record-check fee. That step sits outside the court packet and LegalEase handles neither.

postFilingTimeline.statement: After filing, the prosecuting attorney has 120 days from the date the motion was filed to object and to notify the court and the person. After the judge signs and enters the order, obtain a certified copy of it and confirm that the Oregon State Police sealed its records.
postFilingTimeline.basisQuote: Obtain a certified copy of the order, confirm the Oregon State Police sealed its records, and set expectations that county processing can run many months and in some places close to two years.
postFilingTimeline.expectationNotATiming: The memo also records that county processing can run many months, and in some places close to two years. That is an expectation the packet may set, and it is recorded here as an expectation rather than as a statutory period, because no statute fixes it.
postFilingTimeline.whatItDoesNotSay: No statutory deadline governs when the court must rule after the objection window closes, and none is written.

hearingAndObjectionStops.statement: On a motion under ORS 137.225(1)(c) the court shall grant the motion. If the prosecuting attorney objects within the 120 days, the court holds a hearing at which the victim may make a statement, and the court shall still grant the motion unless it makes written findings by clear and convincing evidence that the person's circumstances and behaviour create a risk to public safety. A prosecutor's objection is a stop condition: the participant is told to get help rather than to argue the hearing from the packet.
hearingAndObjectionStops.basisQuote: Under ORS 137.225(3)(b) the court shall grant a motion under subsection (1)(c) or (1)(d), and shall grant a motion under (1)(a) if no objection is received. If an objection is received the court holds a hearing at which the victim may make a statement, and under ORS 137.225(3)(a) the court shall still grant the motion unless it makes written findings by clear and convincing evidence that the person's circumstances and behaviour create a risk to public safety.
hearingAndObjectionStops.otherRecordedStops: The memo records further stop conditions that belong to screening rather than to this section: establishing a declination date absent from the docket, DUII diversion and traffic-violation dismissals, a pending charge or pending contempt proceeding, multiple counties, federal or out-of-state records, a firearm-rights goal, and immigration exposure.

statutoryAuthority.whyNot: This is the question the 2026-09-20 subsection-authority record resolved as between two committed records, and that record limits itself in terms: it proves what the memo says, not what the enrolled statute says. It records two routes by which statutoryAuthority may be bound -- reading the primary source, or counsel -- and neither has happened. The route id names ORS 137.225(1)(c) while the packet set is or_acquittal, which the memo files under (1)(d), and that disagreement is exactly this section.
statutoryAuthority.doNotInfer: The five sections bound above cite subsections for procedure. That does not bind the controlling subsection for the relief itself, and binding those five must not be read as having settled this one.

copyRequirements.whyNot: The controlling text states no copy count and says nothing about what becomes of each copy. There is no source to bind, and a number invented here would print as fact in a participant's packet.
copyRequirements.whatWouldBindIt: The OJD Criminal Set-Aside (Adult Cases) packet's own filing instructions, or a circuit court's published instructions, read directly.

proposedOrderRule.rule: The proposed order is an OFFICIAL form. ORS 137.225(12) requires the State Court Administrator to publish statewide motion and proposed-order forms, and the retained OJD packet is that set. The packet fills the official proposed order; it never composes one.
proposedOrderRule.theCourtCompletesIt: On entry the order carries the original arrest or citation charge, the conviction charge if different, the date of charge, the submitting agency and the disposition, and directs sealing. The judge signs it, and LegalEase never completes the signature or the court's findings.
proposedOrderRule.consistentWithTheEarlierRecord: The 2026-09-20 record's disposition -- do not draft a custom proposed order -- stands and is reinforced. Binding to the official form is not drafting one. Its proposedOrderGap remains acquisition CLOSED and legalDesign OPEN, and nothing here closes the legal-design question.

specificationNotRegenerated.what: The bindings below are written and the generator now reads them, but data/record-clearing/packet-specifications/OR-set-aside-without-conviction.v1.json has NOT been regenerated, so the committed specification still shows all seven sections unbound.
specificationNotRegenerated.why: scripts/generate-rcap-oregon-packet-specification.mjs refuses at its family-status lookup: the route key is not in data/rcap-ledger/packet-family-build-status.json. That ledger carries 109 rows and not one OR: row of any kind, so this is an absence rather than a key-format drift.
specificationNotRegenerated.provenPreExisting: The unmodified generator from HEAD fails identically at the same line with the same message. The binding wiring added here begins below that line and cannot reach it.
specificationNotRegenerated.notFixedHere: Why Oregon is absent from the family-status ledger is a separate question. It is recorded rather than investigated, and the specification is not hand-edited: it is a generated artifact and writing bound sections into it by hand would produce exactly the unapproved statement this generator exists to prevent.

statusOfThisRecord.readThisFirst: Five of seven does not make the specification composable. legalSectionsBound stays false while any section is unbound, so no packet may be composed from this specification and no route may be proven on it. That is the intended behaviour, not a gap to route around.
statusOfThisRecord.opensNoRoute: The route remains INCOMPLETE and not_commercially_eligible.

whatRemains: statutoryAuthority: read the enrolled ORS 137.225 primary source, or obtain counsel's determination.
copyRequirements: read the OJD packet's filing instructions or a circuit court's published instructions.
Counsel review of all five bound sections before any of them prints to a participant.
remainingReview: Counsel review. This record binds section text from committed controlling material; it composes no packet, approves no output and opens no route.
